Tidying

Filler words“Um”, “uh”, “you know”, and words said twice
CorrectionsChange your mind mid-sentence, or say “scratch that”
Most accurate dictationWhen Whisper and Windows' own recognizer hear something differently, a larger speech model hears it again and settles it (English; about 550 MB, fetched once). Only those few take a few seconds longer
Smart punctuationQuestions get their question mark, and a pause doesn’t end your sentence
Polish with the brainEvery sentence tidied by the AI on this PC. A second or two slower

Look & feel

How ULTRON looks, and the character in the notch.

Follow cursorEyes track your pointer
Blinking
Eye size
Eye speed
Show name when minimized
Body
Menu barHidden, it slides away and comes back when you rest the pointer on the top edge of the screen
Settings styleHow this window looks: ULTRON’s own glass, or macOS’s System Settings
Rounded windowsEvery window gets rounded corners, maximised ones too: their top corners curve into the menu bar and their bottom corners round off, like a Mac’s screen
Glass dialogsWindows’ message boxes (“Save changes?”) appear as ULTRON’s own glass ones
ULTRON’s volume and brightnessShown under the notch instead of Windows’ own box when you press the volume keys
Four-finger swipeSwipe four fingers left or right to slide between windows: in Windows’ touchpad settings, under Four-finger gestures, choose Custom shortcut and press Ctrl+Alt+→ (right) and Ctrl+Alt+← (left). Needs ULTRON’s Alt+Tab on.
ULTRON’s Alt+TabYour open windows as glass cards. Alt+Tab, or hold Alt and scroll (mouse or two fingers on the touchpad); Ctrl+Alt+← / → hops to the next window. Full-screen games keep Windows’ own.
Desktop switchMoving to another of Windows’ desktops, or making a new one, shows which one you’re on
Spatial wallpaperYour wallpaper as a scene with depth, leaning as you move the pointer, on the desktop and the lock screen (the nearest part comes in front of the clock). Worked out on this PC, once per wallpaper
Glass edges bend lightLike real glass, and Apple's: what passes under a panel's rim curves into it. Costs next to nothing
GlassHazelnut is deep and vivid, the colours behind glowing through, and white words read over anything; Clear shows more of what's behind, and its words turn dark over bright pages
Creamy keysEverything you type and every click sounds like a keyboard with creamy switches (real recordings of NovelKeys Creams)
Sound volume
Pointer motion blurA soft streak trails the pointer when it moves fast
Lock screenULTRON’s is your wallpaper and the time, under glass. It comes up from Lock Screen in the ULTRON menu; Win L stays Windows’ own.
ClockGlass shows your wallpaper through the figures
Clock weight
Clock colour
Battery and weatherUnder the clock, in small pieces of glass
Only ULTRON’s lock screenWhen the PC wakes, Windows won’t ask for its own sign-in first: ULTRON’s comes up instead. Restarts and Win L still use Windows’ sign-in.
PasscodeAsked for on ULTRON’s lock screen, in its own glass. It keeps a passer-by out; forget it, and Windows’ sign-in lets you back in.
Then Windows’ own sign-in tooWindows’ screen follows ULTRON’s. That one can’t be restyled: it belongs to Windows, and only it can check your Windows PIN.
See it now
Reduce motionCalmer, shorter animations everywhere
Live glassGlass shows the windows behind it, not just the wallpaper

Taskbar

ULTRON’s own is a wheel that rolls down from under the notch. Nothing sits along the bottom: your windows get the whole screen.

TaskbarWindows’ own comes back, as it was, the moment you switch or ULTRON closes
Start menuULTRON’s opens on the Windows key, and on Ctrl Space: your wallpaper on one side, a search on the other. Windows-key shortcuts all still work.
Ctrl Space opens ULTRON’s StartFrom anywhere, whichever Start the Windows key opens. While it’s on, other apps don’t get Ctrl Space (VS Code’s suggestions, Excel’s column select). Another app has it right now.
The wheel comes downIts sliver sits under the notch
Shortcut for the wheelBrings it down from anywhere, and back up again. Click, then press the keys

Notifications

What your apps tell you, and how it reaches you.

Show themULTRON’s hang down from the menu bar in glass and gather under the bell by the clock, with the same buttons and replies Windows’ have. While they’re on, Windows’ own pop-ups are switched off app by app, and switched back when you choose Windows again or ULTRON closes.
Do not disturbThey still gather under the bell, without coming down
SoundA soft chime as one comes down (not for apps that ask for quiet)
Stay down for
AppsWindows’ own switch for each app that has sent notifications lately
